name: Seeed XIAO ESP32C5
radio: the SoC's own radios: wifi24, wifi5, ble, ieee802154

flash.bootloader_instructions: Hold BOOT while plugging in USB; release after a second. The chip's USB-JTAG-serial port appears.
flash.note: 8 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM per Seeed's spec table (2026-11-23): the same parts as the ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1-N8R8, so that build's partition table fits. Offset 0x2000 is the ESP32-C5 convention; to be confirmed with the first board.

usb.when: ESP32-S3/C5 USB-JTAG-serial (download mode and, with CDC on boot, the running firmware)

pins.name: IO27
pins.note: yellow user LED; IO27 in the DevKitC-1 CircuitPython build's pin names

pins.name: IO6
pins.note: battery voltage through the 1:2 divider (BAT_VOLT_PIN); read only with IO26 high

pins.name: IO28
pins.note: the BOOT button (hold at power-up for the ROM bootloader)

led.note: one yellow user LED on GPIO27 (Seeed: USER_LED). Seeed's example drives the pin LOW for on, so active-low is the expectation; confirm the blink direction on the bench (the firmware does not honour active_low yet)

battery.sense: GPIO6 through a 1:2 divider (two 100 k), gated by GPIO26 (BAT_VOLT_PIN_EN must be high to read)
battery.divider_note: the network foxes do not read a battery yet and the gate pin is not driven, so roles.batt_sense stays null; a 3.7 V cell on the pads charges from USB. A USB pack must not have a low-current cut-off, or the board never wakes from deep sleep.

notes: 5 GHz Wi-Fi and an 802.15.4 radio beside the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and BLE. 8 MB PSRAM: expect a mem= in the megabytes, as on the S3 (the C3's 36 KB is not this board's problem). Reset is CHIP_EN (the R button), Boot is GPIO28 (the B button).
Power: a fox sleeps between transmissions; a USB power bank with a low-current auto-off cuts power during the sleep and the fox never wakes. Use a pack without auto-off.
Serial: native USB — the console port disappears while the chip sleeps and returns when it wakes. 'serial port dropped' each cycle is expected.

circuitpython.note: CircuitPython has no XIAO ESP32C5 build (checked 2026-10-24 and again 2026-11-23: only the DevKitC-1-N8R8 and a Waveshare display board); the ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1-N8R8 build is the same chip with the same 8 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM and runs here, reporting espressif_esp32c5_devkitc_1_n8r8 — the same id the FireBeetle 2 ESP32-C5 reports, so the page keeps whichever of the two is selected. Pin names are the DevKit's IOxx. To verify on the board.
